full_judgment:
3. The property covered by RS Plot No. 509 under RS Khatian No. 603 measuring an area of 0.03 decimals originally belonged to Shayama Charan Biswas and 7 others. Accordingly, RS Khatian stand recorded in their names with a remark in the remark column that the said land is pathway. Shayama Charan Biswas died leaving brother Amullya Ranjan who also died leaving three sons, defendant Nos. 1-3. Other RS recorded owners namely, Manoranjan, Hriday Ranjan and Dinesh Chandra sold their share to the predecessor of the plaintiffs but they could not execute sale deed in favour of the plaintiff’s predecessor as they left the country for India. RS recorded owner Kali kumar died leaving only son Tejendra Kumar who also died leaving four sons, the defendant Nos. 4-7. Another RS recordee Sarada died leaving behind his brother Jitendra who also died leaving four sons, the defendant Nos. 8-11. During BS operation Amullya Ranjan son of Tripura Charan managed to get the suit land recorded in his name in collusion with settlement staffs which was disclosed by his heirs, defendant Nos. 1-3 recently. Though BS Khatian stands recorded in the name of Amullya Ranjan the right of pathway of the plaintiffs were not in any way disturbed by anybody. The homestead of the plaintiffs situated in RS Plot Nos. 505, 506, 507, 508 and 508/1341. The plaintiffs have been using the suit land from the period of their predecessors as their only pathway. Without the suit pathway the plaintiffs have no alternative pathway to go out from their homestead. By using the pathway from time immemorial the plaintiffs have acquired easement right over the same. On 1-5-1995, the defendants threatened the plaintiffs that they will make obstruction on the pathway, hence the present suit. 

 6. Ms Jhuma Halder, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the plaintiffs claim is easement right of necessity and by user. The trial court as well as the appellate court below committed an error of law in not considering whether the plaintiffs have been using the suit pathway for ingress and egress from their homestead and got an easement by user of the same and by necessity. She further submits that the courts below have failed to hold that the suit plot recorded in RS and BS khatians as pathway for the use of both the parties as adjacent and nearby plot owners and co-sharer by purchase from RS recorded owner Manoronjan and others and by using the suit pathway for long time the plaintiffs have acquired right to pathway for the purpose of ingress and egress from their house but the courts below in not considering this aspect of the case committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. It is also argued that the Advocate Commissioner in its investigation report submitted before the trial court specifically mentioned that the plaintiffs have no other alternative pathway except the suit land to go out from their homestead. Moreover, in the remark column of BS Khatian it has been specifically mentioned that the pathway is meant for the use of the occupiers of nearby plots. The northern tank bank of the pond connecting to the plaintiffs homestead towards public road situated in the west of the pond is not a pathway and the plaintiffs never used the tank bank for the purpose of ingress and egress of their homestead. Ms Halder also submits that this is the only way to reach the main road from their residence but both the courts below most unfortunately failed to appreciate the said facts of the instant case and, as such, the judgment and decree of the courts below are liable to be set aside. In support of her submissions she has referred to the cases of Raychand Vanmalidas vs Maneklal mansukhbhai, AIR 1946 Bombay 266 and Abdul Aziz vs Mojahid Ali, 44 DLR 511, the facts of those cases are substantially different from the case in hand. 

 8. It is also argued that the plaintiffs particularly PW 1 in his examination-in-chief as well as in the plaint tried to make out a case of right of easement by prescription saying that they have been using the pathway for more than 100 years but such claim of the PW 1 has not been corroborated by other PWs as well as by any documents. He further submits that mere assertion of a right over a pathway simply saying that they have been using the same for more than 100 years cannot establish a right of easement by prescription over the land of servient owner. Mr Rahman further submits that admittedly, the plaintiffs do not belong to the same caste and not co-sharer in the holding and therefore, the comment in the remark column of the khatian does not include the plaintiffs to be occupiers in any nearby plot under the disputed khatian and, as such, the plaintiffs by the said remark in the khatian cannot claim any right of easement over the suit land. Referring to the evidences of PWs 2 and 3 he submits that those witnesses of the plaintiffs unequivocally admitted in cross that the plaintiffs have been using the northern tank bank of plot No. 505 for ingress and egress of their residence. From the said evidences, it is clearly established that the plaintiffs pathway and the defendants pathway are absolutely separate from each other and they never used the suit land as their pathway for ingress and egress of their residence and, as such, both the courts below upon proper appreciation of the evidences on record both oral and documentary found that the plaintiffs have failed to establish their claim of easement over the suit land by any cogent evidence rather found that the plaintiffs have alternative and separate pathway other than the suit land and therefore, the courts below committed no illegality in dismissing the suit as well as the appeal. In support of his submissions he has referred to a catenae of cases Hero Vinoth vs Seshammal, 5 SCC 545, Justiniano Antao vs Smt. Bernadette B. Pereira, AIR 2005 SC 236, Thomas Ambrose vs Ramdas Balmiki, AIR 2013 MP 187, Usarani Das vs Bhaktahari Mohanty, AIR 1984 Orissa 97, Mariyayi Ammal vs Arunachala Pandaram, 1954 Madras 584, and Mohsin Ali Chowdhury vs Muzammel Khan, 42 DLR 167.
